59-61a. Truly often indeed you too: it is told that sorceresses draw down the moon with their spells. The Thessalian women are thought to do this, having failed in their assumption; according to which Aglaonice, daughter of Hegemon, being experienced in astronomy and knowing the eclipses of the moon, whenever they were about to occur, claimed to draw down the goddess,

20 This he says, since it is told that sorceresses draw down the moon with their spells. And especially the Thessalian women are thought to do this, as also Aristophanes (Nub. 749 sq.): 'having bought a Thessalian sorceress woman, I would draw down the moon at night through her' with the rest omitted in A. cf. W 30
and immediately she fell into misfortunes, losing one of her relatives. Whence in life a proverb is said upon 〈...〉 'she draws down the moon'.

b. Remembering love: that of Endymion through your spells. And dark in the moonless night, because of my occupation with the beloved. Some interpret the eclipse of the moon as being caused by sorceresses drawing it down, and the ancients called eclipses 'drawings down'.

Medea does not go out according to her own choice, but to a feast to which the Argonauts were invited by design, when the time for their destruction was at hand, and Aeetes was urged on to intercourse with his wife Eurylyte, Idmon advised the Argonauts to flee, and Medea sailed out with them.
